DB-02-M01.methodTitle: Build an interface people can use
DB-02-M01.introduction: Think of the page in three parts. HTML tells the browser what each element means. CSS decides how it looks and fits. JavaScript changes what happens when somebody interacts with it.
DB-02-M01.method: Build the meaningful structure first. Preview it. Add layout rules, then interaction. Use a real label for each field and a real button for each action. Test with the keyboard and at the requested screen width.
DB-02-M01.commonMistake: A page that looks right can still fail. Check the action, the field error and the small-screen layout, not just the first screenshot.
DB-02-M01.principle: HTML describes meaningful structure, CSS controls layout, and JavaScript handles interaction. Test the result using the isolated preview and retain expected versus actual behavior.

DB-03-M01.methodTitle: Understand a request and its response
DB-03-M01.introduction: An API is a way for one piece of software to ask another piece to do a specific job. A request has an action, an address and sometimes input. The response tells us what happened.

DB-04-M03.methodTitle: Build an interface people can use
DB-04-M03.introduction: Think of the page in three parts. HTML tells the browser what each element means. CSS decides how it looks and fits. JavaScript changes what happens when somebody interacts with it.
DB-04-M03.method: Build the meaningful structure first. Preview it. Add layout rules, then interaction. Use a real label for each field and a real button for each action. Test with the keyboard and at the requested screen width.
DB-04-M03.commonMistake: A page that looks right can still fail. Check the action, the field error and the small-screen layout, not just the first screenshot.
DB-04-M03.principle: HTML describes meaningful structure, CSS controls layout, and JavaScript handles interaction. Test the result using the isolated preview and retain expected versus actual behavior.

DB-04-M04.methodTitle: Prepare something another person can use
DB-04-M04.introduction: We are creating a usable piece of professional work. A long paragraph is not enough. The person receiving it needs to know what to do, who owns the next action and how to check the result.
DB-04-M04.method: Start with the requested outcome. Add the source facts, decision, owner, check and next action. Keep assumptions visible. Write one clear section at a time, then check that every required section is present.
DB-04-M04.commonMistake: A structure check can detect missing sections. It cannot decide whether your advice is professionally sound; a qualified person must review that.
DB-04-M04.principle: Generated work should be reviewed, tested and attributed as appropriate. Do not claim execution or correctness without evidence.

DB-05-M01.methodTitle: Ask a precise question of a table
DB-05-M01.introduction: A table holds rows of facts. SQL is a language for asking which facts you want. We will use a small, documented trainer, so you can see the result directly beside the source.
DB-05-M01.method: Name the columns you need with SELECT and the table with FROM. Add WHERE to keep only matching rows. Add ORDER BY when the order matters. Run the query and compare every result with the source.
DB-05-M01.commonMistake: A query can run successfully and still answer the wrong question. Check its meaning, selected rows and total before accepting it.
DB-05-M01.principle: A relation is a table of consistently shaped records. SELECT projects rows and columns. The local query trainer implements a documented subset; production PostgreSQL setup is separate.

DB-07-M01.methodTitle: Give each person only the access they need
DB-07-M01.introduction: Permissions answer two questions: what action may this person take, and on whose records? We will use the stated role policy rather than assuming that every signed-in person can do everything.
DB-07-M01.method: Read the role policy. For each action, choose deny, own records, assigned records or all records. Run the matrix checks, then try the case where the person should be refused.
DB-07-M01.commonMistake: A verifier checks evidence. In this case, that responsibility does not include changing the underlying booking.
DB-07-M01.principle: Least privilege grants only the access required for the current role and record context.

DB-07-M02.methodTitle: Understand a request and its response
DB-07-M02.introduction: An API is a way for one piece of software to ask another piece to do a specific job. A request has an action, an address and sometimes input. The response tells us what happened.
DB-07-M02.method: Choose the method and resource path. Check who is making the request. Send it and inspect the status and returned data. Then try the invalid and wrong-owner cases. A successful status alone is not enough.

DB-07-M02.principle: An identifier that can be guessed must still be protected by ownership checks.

DB-08-M01.objective: Test form acceptance and failure behavior
DB-08-M01.methodTitle: Build an interface people can use
DB-08-M01.introduction: Think of the page in three parts. HTML tells the browser what each element means. CSS decides how it looks and fits. JavaScript changes what happens when somebody interacts with it.
DB-08-M01.method: Build the meaningful structure first. Preview it. Add layout rules, then interaction. Use a real label for each field and a real button for each action. Test with the keyboard and at the requested screen width.
DB-08-M01.commonMistake: A page that looks right can still fail. Check the action, the field error and the small-screen layout, not just the first screenshot.
DB-08-M01.principle: A test is a reproducible action with an expected result. Passing appearance checks does not prove behavior.

DB-08-M02.methodTitle: Understand a request and its response
DB-08-M02.introduction: An API is a way for one piece of software to ask another piece to do a specific job. A request has an action, an address and sometimes input. The response tells us what happened.
DB-08-M02.method: Choose the method and resource path. Check who is making the request. Send it and inspect the status and returned data. Then try the invalid and wrong-owner cases. A successful status alone is not enough.

DB-08-M02.principle: Boundary tests target the edge of an allowed input domain, not only a typical value.

DB-10-M01.principle: Arrival order can differ from business revision order. Keep monotonic revisions to avoid restoring stale state.

DB-12-M01.introduction: Automation means applying a sequence of rules consistently. Before an action can have an effect, we need valid input, duplicate protection, the required human approval and a record of what happened.
DB-12-M01.method: Define the steps in their required order. Set a small retry limit and a positive waiting time. Name the owner who receives failures when the retry limit is reached. Run the normal and missing-input cases.

steps.title: First, understand the job
steps.body: Let’s work on this task: map a controlled order workflow. Here is your client or operating brief: Configure Validate → Check duplicate → Human approval → Record result for a fictional order.

steps.title: Here is the method

DB-12-M04.methodTitle: Prepare something another person can use
DB-12-M04.introduction: We are creating a usable piece of professional work. A long paragraph is not enough. The person receiving it needs to know what to do, who owns the next action and how to check the result.
DB-12-M04.method: Start with the requested outcome. Add the source facts, decision, owner, check and next action. Keep assumptions visible. Write one clear section at a time, then check that every required section is present.
DB-12-M04.commonMistake: A structure check can detect missing sections. It cannot decide whether your advice is professionally sound; a qualified person must review that.
DB-12-M04.principle: Separate suggestion from authorization. Human approval should occur before consequential external actions.

DB-13-M03.methodTitle: Give each person only the access they need
DB-13-M03.introduction: Permissions answer two questions: what action may this person take, and on whose records? We will use the stated role policy rather than assuming that every signed-in person can do everything.
DB-13-M03.method: Read the role policy. For each action, choose deny, own records, assigned records or all records. Run the matrix checks, then try the case where the person should be refused.
DB-13-M03.commonMistake: A verifier checks evidence. In this case, that responsibility does not include changing the underlying booking.
DB-13-M03.principle: Record permissions depend on role, ownership and purpose, especially for private employee data.

DB-14-M03.method: Read the feed in its arrival order. Enable the newer-revision rule and repeated-ID rule. Process the feed and inspect each decision. The final state must come from the newest accepted revision.

DB-14-M03.principle: A mobile client should resynchronize with authoritative state instead of assuming its cached state is current.

LEARN.title: Understand the method

TRY.title: Make a small first attempt

BUILD.title: Do the complete job

BREAK.title: Find a failure safely

DB-17-M02.methodTitle: Build an interface people can use
DB-17-M02.introduction: Think of the page in three parts. HTML tells the browser what each element means. CSS decides how it looks and fits. JavaScript changes what happens when somebody interacts with it.
DB-17-M02.method: Build the meaningful structure first. Preview it. Add layout rules, then interaction. Use a real label for each field and a real button for each action. Test with the keyboard and at the requested screen width.
DB-17-M02.commonMistake: A page that looks right can still fail. Check the action, the field error and the small-screen layout, not just the first screenshot.
DB-17-M02.principle: HTML describes meaningful structure, CSS controls layout, and JavaScript handles interaction. Test the result using the isolated preview and retain expected versus actual behavior.

DB-17-M03.methodTitle: Understand a request and its response
DB-17-M03.introduction: An API is a way for one piece of software to ask another piece to do a specific job. A request has an action, an address and sometimes input. The response tells us what happened.
DB-17-M03.method: Choose the method and resource path. Check who is making the request. Send it and inspect the status and returned data. Then try the invalid and wrong-owner cases. A successful status alone is not enough.
DB-17-M03.commonMistake: Knowing a record ID does not give you permission to see it. Also, retrying a request must not create the same booking twice.
DB-17-M03.principle: The interface and request service need a shared data contract.

TRY.nextAction: Run a small attempt and record what it revealed.

BUILD.title: Do the complete job
BUILD.spoken: You have seen the method and tried a small part. Now produce the full requested result. Use the case facts, run the current checks and finish the operating actions where this mission requires them.
BUILD.nextAction: Build the requested result and resolve the failed checks.

BREAK.title: Find a failure safely
BREAK.spoken: Let’s see whether your control holds when something goes wrong. Run the supplied failure test and inspect its actual result. We want to know why the bad input was refused, or why it slipped through.
BREAK.nextAction: Run the controlled failure test and explain its cause.

FIX.title: Correct and check again
FIX.spoken: Choose the problem you observed. Make a focused correction, or verify the control that already refused the bad input. Run the work again after the failure test and keep the result.
FIX.nextAction: Describe the correction or confirmed control and keep a successful retest.

TEST.title: Prove the result
TEST.spoken: Now repeat the checks on the current version of your work. Compare the expected result with the actual result. Include one normal case and one failure case so another person can repeat your check.
TEST.nextAction: Run the current checks and record expected versus actual behavior.

EXPLAIN.title: Explain your decision

EXPLAIN.nextAction: Explain your choice, the evidence behind it and its limit.

DEFEND.title: Answer a reviewer’s questions

DEFEND.nextAction: Answer each review question using your own work and test evidence.

SHIP.title: Hand over usable work

SHIP.nextAction: Export the current work and write the handover instructions.

DB-21-M03.introduction: Automation means applying a sequence of rules consistently. Before an action can have an effect, we need valid input, duplicate protection, the required human approval and a record of what happened.

DB-21-M03.principle: An operating workflow should preserve ownership and a recoverable failure path.

DB-22-M02.methodTitle: Build an interface people can use
DB-22-M02.introduction: Think of the page in three parts. HTML tells the browser what each element means. CSS decides how it looks and fits. JavaScript changes what happens when somebody interacts with it.
DB-22-M02.method: Build the meaningful structure first. Preview it. Add layout rules, then interaction. Use a real label for each field and a real button for each action. Test with the keyboard and at the requested screen width.
DB-22-M02.commonMistake: A page that looks right can still fail. Check the action, the field error and the small-screen layout, not just the first screenshot.
DB-22-M02.principle: HTML describes meaningful structure, CSS controls layout, and JavaScript handles interaction. Test the result using the isolated preview and retain expected versus actual behavior.

DB-22-M03.objective: Respond to an injected duplicate incident
DB-22-M03.methodTitle: Understand a request and its response
DB-22-M03.introduction: An API is a way for one piece of software to ask another piece to do a specific job. A request has an action, an address and sometimes input. The response tells us what happened.
DB-22-M03.method: Choose the method and resource path. Check who is making the request. Send it and inspect the status and returned data. Then try the invalid and wrong-owner cases. A successful status alone is not enough.
DB-22-M03.commonMistake: Knowing a record ID does not give you permission to see it. Also, retrying a request must not create the same booking twice.
DB-22-M03.principle: An injected incident tests how a learner adapts under a changed constraint, not only whether a prepared example runs.

BREAK.title: Find a failure safely
